EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE
  MEETING MINUTES
  AUGUST 28, 2017

CALL TO ORDER
CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ called the meeting to order, the time being 7:00 p.m. in the Rolling Hills
Estates City Council Chambers.

COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT
Chairman Velveth Schmitz
Susan Brtis
William Kemp
Lou Persichina
Carrie Silvano
Vicki Shinn
Tim Zigrang

COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT
Carol Dean-Porter
Patricia Harik

ALSO PRESENT
Mayor Frank V. Zerunyan
Richard Tagore-Erwin, R3 Consulting
Alexa Davis, Assistant to the City Manager

APPROVAL OF MINUTES
Minutes of the last meeting were not provided for review and adoption; the item will be placed
upon the September Meeting Agenda.

AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA
MEMBER SHINN promoted the City Celebration on Saturday, September 23. She explained
the events that will be held will include horses as well as games without horses. MEMBER
SHINN also promoted the event at the Empty Saddle Club the night before, Friday,
September 22, to kick-off the City Celebration event.

DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. WASTE MANAGEMENT  CONTRACT  RENEWAL  –  MANURE  SERVICE
  OVERVIEW

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
AUGUST 28, 2017  1
 CHAIR SCHMITZ introduced MAYOR ZERUNYAN and Consultant from R3 Consulting,
RICHARD TAGORE – ERWIN.

CONSULTANT, RICHARD TAGORE – ERWIN, provided a historical overview of current
Waste Management contract. MR. TAGORE – ERWIN explained that in 2004 the City went
to, competitive bid with three proposals and Waste Management (hereafter referred to as
WM) was most competitive with the services.

MR. TAGORE – ERWIN further explained that the expectation in a new contract is to create
a more programmatic approach on the manure, carts or bins and to City municipal stables,
commercial entities or private stables. He continued that in an audit of the contract service,
has been on point, but it was realized that WM has been losing money on the contract. He
stated that manure collection has been the biggest area of loss to them. MR. TAGORE-
ERWIN detailed that the cost of taking manure to facilities has increased in price,
complicated by billing errors done by WM on scout services.

CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that there are 60 manure accounts that receive scout service.
CHAIR SCHMITZ summarized that the City’s Franchise Agreement stipulates the scout
service charge correctly, but the billing was not implemented correctly. She further explained
that in looking at a new contract and the feasibility of continuing the service, rates will need
to be adjusted going forward.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN provided a historic overview of the franchise bidding process. MAYOR
ZERUNYAN explained that in 2004, the City spent eight months looking into a waste
contract, which ultimately led to WM. He explained that the process was also policy driven
to include:
  • One day pick-up with a controlled number of trucks and weight to help with the wear
  and tear on roads.
  • Uniform bins across the City. CHAIR SCHMITZ passed around "before" pictures from
  before WM had the City contract.
  • AB949, which has required waste diversion mandates in effect
  • Unlimited recyclables and greenwaste collection, which at the time helped with
  diversion rates and gave expanded service to residents

MAYOR ZERUNYAN stated that this was an amazing contract when first entered, but now
things have changed related to mandates, such as recyclables are not as valuable and
green waste is more of a burden to haulers. MAYOR ZERUNYAN explained that the City
receives very little complaints of WM and there is a great service to residents, WM supports
community events. He explained that the City is seeking the Committee’s help to engage the
equestrian community since a new contract is likely to disproportionately affect them. He
further stated that based on policy, the City Council answers to 8,000 residents and to be
fair to the non- equestrians, the goal is to keep a rate increase at a minimum, and will not be
able to continue a subsidize manure services

MEMBER KEMP asked if the charge on the regular service will be increased. MAYOR
ZERUNYAN responded that regular residential service is likely to increase but at a
minimum.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
AUGUST 28, 2017  2
 CHAIR SCHMITZ explained that there are considerations to keep rates down as the City is
still in negotiation discussions for a new contract.

MEMBER ZIGRANG asked if WM can drop manure service. MAYOR ZERUNYAN responded
that they have the ability to drop the service but it is very unlikely.

CHAIR SCHMITZ explained that there are greater policy decisions to be considered as well
as general services and clarified that all trucks run on Certified Natural Gas and carry a lighter
load than normally allowed in order to help alleviate street wear and tear. She further
explained that manure has phosphorus and the City has responsibility for storm water
requirements, which makes the manure disposal service a very important discussion.

MEMBER SHINN asked if WM would request a retro payment from existing customers to
correct the billing error. MAYOR ZERUNYAN and MR. TAGORE-ERWIN affirmed that WM
will absorb the cost and look to correct only in a new contract moving forward.

Audience member Mrs. Pam Schachter clarified that this issue does not affect those who
wheel their own bins out for collection. Mr. TAGORE-ERWIN responded affirmatively.

Audience member Mr. Phil More asked for clarification that the error in billing was not related
to full manure service, which would triple his manure service bill. MAYOR ZERUNYAN
responded that only the portion of scout service is affected and will be corrected.

MEMBER SILVANO asked if there will be an overall increase on other rates. MR. TAGORE
ERWINE explained the renewal impacts all city services, including commercial rates and in a
new contract the City is trying to level rates as much as possible and spread it over time.

MEMBER SILVANO asked if residents can control costs by managing their own waste
through recycling efforts; she further expressed concern that a big spike in manure costs can
affect property values.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN clarified that the rates themselves will not have a significant increase.
He further explained that the City is trying to distribute and phase it in an effort to make it as
fair as possible.

MR. TAGORE-ERWIN explained that the value of the contract is ~$2 million per year and WM
has been losing $200,000 per year. He specifically expressed that his clients are public
agencies only, but further explained that to get WM whole in the contract with a small profit,
there should be an 8% margin. MR. TAGORE-ERWIN continued to explain that most margins
are closer to 12% and the ultimate goal is to recognize an increase of ~$300,000, and with
Scout Collection the revenue needs to go from $36,000 to over $100,000 by correcting the
billing error.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
AUGUST 28, 2017  3
 Audience Member Mr. More asked if scout service were to stop, if the City should expect
illegal dumping. The Committee had a general discussion on impacts of illegal dumping.
CHAIR SCHMITZ explained that the City must be in compliance with storm water regulations.

MR. TAGORE-ERWIN summarized that the overall goal is to spread out the revenue gap and
the best way to accomplish that is by: 1) billing scout service correction, 2) have a modest
increase on regular manure collection because for processing costs have increased, and 3)
consider limiting green waste to some extent because organics have disposal has increased
as a result of AB 1826 and mandatory organics waste.

MEMBER SILVANO asked if private facilities will continue to not be required to use
WM. MAYOR ZERUNYAN responded that it is still uncertain as the City is trying to find the
right balance between service, rates and policy impacts, such as storm water requirements.

Audience member asked if scout bin service was going to go up a minimum of $45 per month
with the correction in billing. MR. TAGORE-ERWIN responded that that amount is likely.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN asked the committee and audience for feedback on if the City were to
limit green waste and/or recycling bins. The group agreed that limiting the current free
services to 2-4 carts with a charge for bins used beyond an established limit would be a fair
compromise if it could keep minimize a general rate increase.

CHAIR SCHMITZ commented on the positive relationship the City has had with WM and
explained that going out to bid could end up being a more costly approach, especially for
manure service.

MEMBER SHINN expressed that WM drivers are very polite and respectful of equestrian
community and horses.

Audience member asked if the options allowed for an increased to be spread across all
services evenly. MAYOR ZERUNYAN responded affirmatively, but further explained that the
whole community should not bear the full burden for small populations of service
provided.

MEMBER PERSICHINA asked if people are abusing the free bins. MR. TAGORE- ERWIN
responded affirmatively.

MEMBER SILVANO expressed that the equestrians should not subsidize green waste costs.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN and CHAIR SCHMIITZ announced there would be an all-community
meeting on September 19 at 7pm. CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that any potential equestrian
impacts will be shared with the community and Committee.

MEMBER SILVANO stated that equestrians may not be disproportionately affected by
changes in a new contract, but should recognize they were disproportionately benefitted.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
AUGUST 28, 2017  4
 Audience member sked if WM received their increased revenue if the City could remove
manure service from the contract. MAYOR ZERUNYAN explained that removing manure
service from the contract may not help the City meet policy goals and state mandates.

CHAIR SCHMITZ thanked everyone and encouraged that they help keep the conversation
going, to email her or the Mayor with questions and invite them to talk to community. She
expressed that a lot of education and conversation will continue. CHAIR SCHMITZ reminded
everyone abut the City Celebration on September 23, the Community Meeting o September
19 and the next Equestrian Meeting on September 25.

COMMITTEE MEMBER REPORTS
None.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS
None.

ADJOURNMENT
CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 8:25 P.M.

Respectfully submitted,
ALEXA DAVIS
Assistant to the City Manager

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
AUGUST 28, 2017  5
